title: Keep one packer's label out of another's

blocks.text: The warehouse prints shipping labels on several packing lines. Each line has one `LabelPrinter`, and every packer on the line renders labels with it from their own thread. Last month someone made the printer reuse a single buffer for every label "to save allocations". Since then a few parcels a day go out with one customer's name above another customer's street. The postcode lookup goes to a remote service and can take seconds, so a label waiting for its city must not hold up the other packers.

items: `render(...)`: the three lines of one label, counted for the dashboard;
`renderedByAll()`: the number the dashboard shows, every label that any printer has rendered since the service started.

blocks.text: About eight lines in total. The tests render labels from several threads on one printer, and on several printers one after the other.

cases.says: each label has the name, the street, and the postcode with its city, and every label adds one to the count
a label rendered while another packer's label waits for its city comes out complete, and the waiting label keeps its own lines
the count includes the labels of every printer, also those rendered before another printer was created

origin.section: A Static Field Is One Variable Shared by Every Object and Every Thread

concepts: final on a static field fixes the reference, not the object, so a mutable object in it is shared by concurrent callers; immutable or concurrent objects are safe there.
A static field is one variable for the whole class, read and written by every object and every thread that uses the class.
